suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Case-sensitivity bypass in blacklist check: blacklistedGuestEmails are normalized to lower case (line 71 .toLowerCase()) but the incoming guest is compared without normalization via blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) at line 77. An attacker can bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS by submitting Blocked@Example.com vs blocked@example.com. Fix: normalize guest to lower case before comparison (and for the duplicate check), e.g., guest.toLowerCase() === attendee.email.toLowerCase() and blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest.toLowerCase()).

suggestions.label: security

Submitting existing@example.com as Existing@Example.com passes the filter and creates a duplicate attendee record (also defeats the uniqueGuests dedup). Fix: compare lowercased forms: guest.toLowerCase() === attendee.email.toLowerCase().

suggestions.suggestionContent: Cross-reference inconsistency: client AddGuestsDialog.tsx validates guests with .refine(unique) while server ZAddGuestsInputSchema only checks z.array(z.string().email()) with no uniqueness check. Server handler’s filter also doesn’t dedupe duplicates within guests itself, so bypassing client validation can insert duplicate attendee rows via createMany.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Check-then-create race + missing intra-request dedup allows duplicate Attendees and execution break: `uniqueGuests` only filters against existing attendees with case-sensitive `===` and against blacklisted list, but never deduplicates `guests` itself nor normalizes case, and the read (findFirst) and write (booking.update createMany) are non-atomic with no unique constraint handling. Two concurrent addGuests with same email or a single request with ["x@a.com","x@a.com"] or ["X@a.com","x@a.com"] both insert duplicate rows (state corruption) or throw Prisma P2002 unhandled. Fix: normalize to lower-case, dedupe with Set, and make insertion atomic — e.g., add unique index on (bookingId, email) if missing and handle conflict, or use transaction/upsert and validate `uniqueGuests` after normalization.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Server input schema permits duplicate/invalid invariants that client rejects: `z.array(z.string().email())` allows duplicate emails and empty array, unlike client schema which refines `uniqueEmails.size === emails.length`. A crafted request bypasses client and reaches handler with duplicates, causing duplicate createMany (state corruption) or DB unique-constraint exception (unhandled execution break at JSON-encode/Prisma layer). Fix: add `.refine` for uniqueness (and optionally `.nonempty().max(N)`) mirroring client, and normalize emails to lower-case before validation.

suggestions.label: bug

WHY: TokenID format is 6 chars = st(0,2)+tt(2,4)+gt(4,6); code extracts wrong chars and fails when grant matches, passes when it mismatches, so expectCodeToToken etc. never correctly validate. HOW: Use `!items[0].substring(4,6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)` return false; or `if (!...equals(...)) return false;`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: isAccessTokenId matcher does not verify grant type: it checks substring(3,5) instead of (4,6) and inverts the condition `if (equals) return false`. As written it returns true for any token with a valid UUID regardless of grant shortcut, so expectCodeToToken / expectRefresh / expectAuthReqIdToToken would still pass if the wrong grant were encoded. Fix to `if (!items[0].substring(4,6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: isAccessTokenId has wrong offset and inverted logic: it checks items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expected) return false. Prefix is 2+2+2=6, grant shortcut is at 4,6 not 3,5, and should fail when NOT equals. Fix to if (!items[0].substring(4,6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false; otherwise the test will pass for wrong grants and fail for correct grants.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Off-by-one slice: code uses items[0].substring(3,5) but the encoded token layout is 6 chars before ':' where grant shortcut occupies indices 4-5 (session 0-1, token 2-3, grant 4-5). For "trltcc:1234" or "onrtac:UUID", substring(3,5) returns "tc"/"ta" instead of "cc"/"ac". Fix to substring(4,6) (and guard length==6 before slicing).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Inverted comparison: `if (slice.equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false` returns false when the grant DOES match expected and true when it doesn't, so valid tokens fail and invalid grants pass. Should be `if (!slice.equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Generator (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId) encodes grant shortcut at encodedContext[4:6] (session 0-1, token 2-3, grant 4-5) and tests prove format e.g. 'trltcc:1234'. Validator isAccessTokenId extracts items[0].substring(3,5) (off-by-one, yields 1 char of tokenType + 1 char of grant) and inverts the check: `if (substring.equals(expected)) return false`. Fix to `if (!items[0].substring(4,6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` and keep UUID check on items[1].

problems: Environment names are interpolated into Markdown code spans without escaping.
Issue titles are interpolated into Markdown links without escaping.
uncoveredProblems: Unescaped environment names can alter PR-comment Markdown.
Unescaped issue titles can alter PR-comment Markdown links.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: get_environment_info returns raw environment.name interpolated into MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE markdown (` in `{name}`) without escaping, and get_merged_pr_single_issue_template interpolates truncated_title directly into markdown link. WHY: Environment names and issue titles are attacker-controllable (project config / issue title); a value containing `]`, `)`, backticks or markdown can break the link and inject arbitrary markdown links or code spans into GitHub/GitLab PR comments. HOW: Escape markdown special characters in title and environment before formatting.

problems: Existing callers passing arrays are incompatible with the new single-string Visualize constructor.
Always setting stack to 'all' changes the previous stacking semantics.
uncoveredProblems: Existing array-based constructor calls are incompatible with the new constructor.
The previous conditional stacking behavior is lost.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Visualize constructor changed from (yAxes: string[]) to (yAxis: string) and stack logic removed (always 'all'). Any caller still constructing `new Visualize(['count()'])` now stores array as string ("count(),other" -> char handling broken) and stack semantics changed. Add overload/compat handling or migrate remaining call sites (grep `new Visualize\(`).
